outcome: Since 26 January 2024 no event classifies the possible configurations of connected components of M-curves for any degree from 8 upwards, and the degree-8 and degree-9 cases remain open in every source read. The in-window events are: an arXiv preprint (Feb 2026, not peer reviewed as far as found) realising all 121 real schemes of degree-7 plane curves by T-curves, a later version (Jul 2026) asserting that some degree-8 M-schemes are not realisable as T-curves, a seminar-only claim (Apr 2026) that some degree-8 arrangements are not reachable by primitive combinatorial patchworking, a June 2026 preprint classifying arrangements of three lines with a cubic or a single-oval quartic (not M-curves, and the one AI-involved event on this problem), and a July 2026 classification of arrangements of a quartic with three lines. The second part of the named problem (limit cycles) saw a contested 2024 claim of a quadratic bound on the Hilbert number that is disputed in print.
problem_asks: The bullet asks for the complete list of possible configurations of the connected components of M-curves, Hilbert's sixteenth problem as worded on Wikipedia. Parts: (a) for each degree n, which arrangements of components (for even n, ovals and nests; for odd n, the non-contractible component together with the ovals) occur for a nonsingular real plane curve of degree n with the maximal number of components (n-1)(n-2)/2 + 1, i.e. an M-curve; (b) 'possible' means realisable, so the list needs both realisation of each configuration and exclusion of the rest; (c) for all n, not for one degree. Read with the named problem: Hilbert's 1900 first part also covers all real curves of degree n and real surfaces, and the second part asks for a finite upper bound H(n) on limit cycles of planar polynomial vector fields of degree n; the bullet asks neither. Those are recorded as different questions where they appear.

events.what_happened: D. A. Gudkov classified the configurations of M-sextics (nonsingular real plane curves of degree 6 with 11 components). Maletto (arXiv 2606.21449, section 1.2.1, 2026) states: 'd = 6: classified by Gudkov in 1969, after Hilbert's incomplete 1902-era work'. Secondary search summaries also say Gudkov disproved one of Hilbert's conjectures on oval arrangements in plane M-sextics. The 1969 paper itself was not opened.
events.delivers: Complete list of the configurations of M-curves of degree 6, as stated in the 2026 Maletto paper's history. Restricted to degree 6.
events.remains: Nothing for degree 6 according to the cited sources.
events.directly_checkable: Degree-6 M-configurations can be checked against the Gudkov-Rokhlin congruence and by patchworking; not checked by me.
events.direction: Positive classification for degree 6.

events.what_happened: O. Ya. Viro classified the real schemes of smooth real plane curves of degree 7: 121 schemes in total for all smooth curves, of which the degree-7 M-schemes form a subset. Sources disagree on the year: Maletto (arXiv 2606.21449, section 1.2.1) says 'd = 7: classified by Viro in 1979'; Geiselmann et al. (arXiv 2602.06888 v1, 2026) cite Viro (1984). The original papers were not opened.
events.revisions: Year disputed between sources: 1979 (Maletto 2026) and 1984 (Geiselmann et al. 2026).
events.delivers: Complete list of real schemes of smooth degree-7 plane curves (121), which includes all degree-7 M-schemes. Restricted to degree 7. A secondary survey summary (not verified in a primary source) says the M-curve classification is complete through degree 7.
events.remains: Nothing at degree 7 according to the cited sources. Whether each scheme is realised by algebraic curves is a separate matter; see the 2026 T-curve event for the realisation by T-curves.
events.direction: Positive classification for degree 7.

events.what_happened: S. Yu. Orevkov, 'New M-curve of degree 8' (Funktsional. Anal. i Prilozhen. 36:3, 2002; English Funct. Anal. Appl. 36:3, 2002, pp. 247-249, per a search summary). It constructs an algebraic M-curve of degree 8 with 22 ovals realising an isotopy type whose realisability was previously unknown. The note was not opened; the description comes from search summaries and from Orevkov's degree-8 classification page.
events.delivers: Algebraic realisation of one degree-8 M-scheme (22 ovals). Per the same secondary report, six arrangements of 22 ovals remained whose M-realisability was unknown. Restricted to degree 8.
events.remains: The six remaining degree-8 arrangements of 22 ovals whose algebraic realisability was unknown (per the secondary report).
events.direction: Positive algebraic realisation of one degree-8 M-scheme; leaves a short list open.
events.object: An algebraic (not only pseudo-holomorphic) M-curve of degree 8 with 22 ovals, realising an isotopy type previously unknown to be realisable. The equation is in the note, which was not read. Explicit, as far as the summaries say.

events.what_happened: S. Yu. Orevkov, 'Classification of flexible M-curves of degree 8 up to isotopy' (author's abstract page, undated). It completes the classification of real pseudo-holomorphic M-curves on RP^2 of degree 8 up to isotopy. Two schemes are excluded (1 U 1<3> U 1<16> and 1 U 1<13> U 1<6>); seven are shown realisable as real point sets of pseudo-holomorphic M-curves of degree 8 (1 U 1<1> U 1<18>, 1 U 1<4> U 1<15>, 1 U 1<7> U 1<12>, 1 U 1<9> U 1<10>, 4 U 1<2 U 1<14>>, 14 U 1<2 U 1<4>>, 7 U 1<2 U 1<11>>). Method: braid restriction plus periodicity of Tristram signatures, degeneration, and an Alexander-polynomial analogue of Fox-Milnor. The publication year is not on the page; a search summary gives GAFA 2002, and Brugallé's April 2004 arXiv paper (math/0404030) cites the classification as achieved.
events.revisions: Year not confirmed on the page. The 2002 date is a secondary summary's reading of the journal (GAFA); the paper is cited as achieved in Brugallé's 2004 arXiv paper.
events.delivers: For degree-8 M-curves in RP^2 up to isotopy, in the pseudo-holomorphic category only: two schemes excluded and seven realised, and the list of pseudo-holomorphically realisable types is complete. Restricted to pseudo-holomorphic curves, so it does not by itself decide algebraic realisability.
events.remains: Algebraic realisability of the degree-8 M-schemes that are pseudo-holomorphically realisable but not known to be algebraic. A secondary report (Brugallé 2004, not read) says six schemes remain for which algebraic realisability is unknown. The 2026 sources read (Maletto; Geiselmann et al. v3; ZIB project page) all still call degree 8 open.
events.doubts: The classification is pseudo-holomorphic, while the bullet asks about algebraic M-curves; the status sources differ on which setting they mean (see disputes).
events.direction: Obstructions for two degree-8 schemes; realisations for seven in the pseudo-holomorphic category; leaves the algebraic question for some schemes open.
events.object: Seven pseudo-holomorphic M-curves of degree 8 realising the listed schemes, and two excluded schemes (1 U 1<3> U 1<16> and 1 U 1<13> U 1<6>) ruled out by braid-monodromy and Tristram-signature arguments. The realising curves are pseudo-holomorphic, not algebraic. Non-constructive or constructive status of the seven is not stated in the abstract page.

events.what_happened: S. Fiedler-Le Touze, 'M-curves of degree 9 with deep nests' (2006; revised 2008, per secondary summaries). It prohibits isotopy types of degree-9 M-curves with a nest of depth 3 and no outer ovals: 10 types in the first version and 13 in a later one, per a search summary. Korchagin's conjecture on deep nests remains open. Not opened; the 2008 arXiv entry is the one read.
events.revisions: Revised 2008 (per secondary summary), with the excluded-type count changing from 10 to 13.
events.delivers: Partial exclusion of degree-9 M-configurations with deep nests and no outer ovals (10 or 13 types, depending on version). Restricted to degree 9 and to that nest pattern.
events.remains: Degree-9 M-configurations in general, and the deep-nest case in full (Korchagin's conjecture).
events.direction: Obstruction for a restricted class of degree-9 M-curves.

events.what_happened: F. Bertrand, E. Brugallé and G. Renaudineau, 'Haas' theorem revisited' (arXiv 1609.01979, 2016). It gives an alternative proof of B. Haas's classification of the M-curves produced by unimodular combinatorial patchworking (Haas's thesis). Arxiv abstract not opened; description from a search snippet and from a citation in a search summary.
events.delivers: Classification of M-curves that come from unimodular combinatorial patchworking, a restricted construction class. Not a classification of all M-curves.
events.remains: All M-curves not produced by unimodular combinatorial patchworking, including the degree-8 cases above.
events.direction: Classification within a restricted construction class.

events.what_happened: S. Fiedler-Le Touze, 'M-curves of degree 9 with three nests' (arXiv 0806.4446, submitted 27 Jun 2008, last revised 14 Sep 2010). Proves that at least one of the numbers alpha_i of empty ovals in the three nests is odd, a step towards Korchagin's conjecture that at least two are odd. A search summary reports that the arXiv abstract says 41 new isotopy types are excluded; the abstract read did not state that number.
events.delivers: A parity constraint (at least one alpha_i odd) on degree-9 M-curves with three nests. Restricted to degree 9 and to the three-nest case; does not classify.
events.remains: Degree-9 M-configurations in general; the three-nest case beyond the parity result (Korchagin's conjecture).
events.direction: Obstruction (parity constraint) in a restricted degree-9 class.

events.what_happened: Matilde Manzaroli, 'Real plane separating (M-2)-curves of degree d and totally real pencils of degree d-3' (arXiv 2404.09671, first posted April 2024; v4 6 Jan 2026). Published in Epijournal de Geometrie Algebrique, vol. 10 (2026); acceptance 22 Aug 2025 per a search summary. The subject is (M-2)-curves, which have two fewer components than the Harnack maximum (one fewer than M-curves in the standard convention of the search snippet), not M-curves themselves; M-curves appear as background only.
events.revisions: v4 6 Jan 2026 (arXiv); journal version EpiGA 2026 (accepted 22 Aug 2025 per a search summary). The April 2024 date is the month of first posting as given by search summaries; the v1 page was not read.
events.delivers: For separating (M-2)-curves of degree d: existence of infinitely many totally real pencils of degree d-3 with g-1 or g-2 base points on the curve (Theorem 1.9, quoted). Generalises a degree-5 fact on non-convex position of ovals. Scope: (M-2)-curves, not the maximal M-curves the bullet asks about.
events.remains: Everything the bullet asks about M-curves (the maximal component count).

checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted the paper on 22 Aug 2025, per a search summary; the journal page was not opened.

events.direction: Neighbouring question on (M-2)-curves; positive results on separating curves and totally real pencils. No bearing on M-curve configurations found.

events.what_happened: Armengol Gasull and Paulo Santana, 'A note on Hilbert 16th Problem' (arXiv 2407.13465, first submitted 18 Jul 2024; v2 1 Oct 2024). It concerns the second part of Hilbert's 16th problem (limit cycles), not the M-curve question. It shows that H(n) can be realised by structurally stable vector fields with all limit cycles hyperbolic, and that H(n) is strictly increasing whenever it is finite (Theorem 1: H(n+1) >= H(n) + 1).
events.delivers: A structural property of the second-part Hilbert number H(n): strictly increasing where finite, and realisation by hyperbolic structurally stable systems. Gives no upper bound. Scope: second part only.
events.remains: The second part (existence of finite H(n) for n > 1), and the whole M-curve question.
events.direction: Structural result on the second part; neither cuts for nor against an upper bound.

events.what_happened: Vinicius Barros da Silva, Joao Peres Vieira and Edson Denis Leonel, 'Exploring Limit Cycles of Differential Equations through Information Geometry Unveils the Solution to Hilbert's 16th Problem', Entropy 26(9), article 745 (2024). The paper claims that a real polynomial system of degree n >= 2 has at most 2(n-1)(4(n-1)-2) limit cycles (the second part), obtained from the scalar curvature R of the Fisher information metric on the parameter space and a limit-cycle criterion ('Definition 1'). The paper is about the second part only. The MDPI page, DOAJ page and PMC copy were all unavailable to me (HTTP 403 or a reCAPTCHA page), so the text was not read. The date comes from a DOAJ listing ('Entropy (Aug 2024)') in a search result; a FAPESP record gives 1 Sep 2024.
events.revisions: No arXiv preprint for this paper was found in my searches. Date is the journal's August 2024 issue as shown on DOAJ; the FAPESP record gives 2024-09-01.
events.delivers: Claims an upper bound H(n) <= 2(n-1)(4(n-1)-2) for the second part, quadratic in n. Restricted to planar polynomial vector fields and to the authors' criterion for limit cycles. Scope: second part only.
events.remains: The M-curve question is untouched. For the second part, the claim is disputed (see the next two events), and no published correction was found.
events.doubts: Buzzi and Novaes (arXiv 2411.09594) argue that a quadratic bound contradicts known growth: H(n) grows at least like n^2 log n, and the Li-Chan-Chung sequence of systems (degree 2^k-1, at least S_k limit cycles) exceeds the formula for k >= 35. They also argue the paper's limit-cycle criterion is neither necessary nor sufficient, with explicit examples (Examples 1-4 in their note). The authors' reply (arXiv 2412.01916) says the note misreads their framework. The primary text of the Entropy paper was not read, so I cannot say whether the criterion is stated as they describe.
events.direction: Claims a quadratic upper bound for the second-part Hilbert number, which would be a strong positive result on the second part; the critiques argue it is false. The M-curve bullet is not affected.

events.what_happened: Claudio A. Buzzi and Douglas D. Novaes, 'A note on a recent attempt to solve the second part of Hilbert's 16th Problem' (arXiv 2411.09594, submitted 14 Nov 2024; one version found; math.DS). They argue that the quadratic formula of the Entropy paper contradicts the known growth of H(n), give counterexamples from known families of systems (Li-Chan-Chung sequence, and the sequences of Li et al. Sections 4 and 5), and argue the Entropy limit-cycle criterion is neither necessary nor sufficient for limit cycles (Examples 1-4). The note states that it addresses only the second part.
events.delivers: Refutes the quadratic H(n) formula of the Entropy paper by growth and counterexamples. Does not give a new upper or lower bound on any limit-cycle count. Scope: second part only.
events.remains: The second part's upper bound question, which the note does not settle either way. The M-curve bullet is not addressed.
events.doubts: The authors of the claim reply that the note misreads their work (arXiv 2412.01916). Not a doubt about the note itself.
events.direction: Cuts against the Entropy claim (second part); no effect on M-curves.

events.what_happened: Vinicius Barros da Silva, Joao Peres Vieira and Edson Denis Leonel, 'On the Defense of the Recent Solution to Hilbert's Sixteenth Problem: Clarifying Misinterpretations and the Incorrect Conclusions in Buzzi and Novaes's note' (arXiv 2412.01916, submitted 2 Dec 2024; one version). It defends the Entropy claim, says the covariant formulation of geometric bifurcation theory (GBT) is the basis, and says Buzzi and Novaes's note is 'incorrect and leads to erroneous results' because of a 'superficial reading' and 'omission of critical aspects of the GBT'. Only the abstract page was read.
events.delivers: Defends the second-part bound H(n) <= 2(n-1)(4(n-1)-2) against the note. The abstract states the claim but I did not find a new mathematical result beyond it. Scope: second part only.
events.remains: The second part, and the whole M-curve bullet.
events.doubts: Read at abstract level only; I did not check whether it responds to the specific counterexample families (Li-Chan-Chung) in the note. No journal publication or correction was found in my searches.
events.direction: Defends the second-part quadratic bound; no effect on M-curves.

events.what_happened: Armengol Gasull and Paulo Santana, 'Limit cycles and invariant algebraic curves' (arXiv 2510.11705, v1 13 Oct 2025; v2 22 Dec 2025). Gives lower bounds, in terms of n, for the number of limit cycles of degree-n polynomial vector fields that have a prescribed invariant algebraic curve; when the ovals of that curve are algebraic limit cycles, it gives a recurrence for the Hilbert numbers. Second part only.
events.delivers: Lower bounds on second-part limit-cycle counts for systems with a prescribed invariant curve, and a recurrence for Hilbert numbers under extra hypotheses. Gives no upper bound.
events.remains: The second part's upper bound question; the M-curve bullet.
events.direction: Lower-bound direction on the second part; no upper bound.

events.what_happened: S. Yu. Orevkov and N. D. Puchkova, 'On mutual arrangements of a plane real curve relative to an M-quartic with an oval-snake' (arXiv 2512.06907, 7 Dec 2025; one version). An oval of a real quartic that is a snake around a real curve C_k of degree k forces the union of the real curves to be isotopic to that of C_k with a perturbed doubled conic. The algebraic version: the real parts of S4 and C4 together are isotopic to those of Q and C4 (Theorem 4). Background: Puchkova's earlier work on two M-quartics meeting in 16 points. Published, per a search summary, in Matematicheskie Zametki 119(2), 2026, pp. 253-265 (journal page not opened).
events.delivers: A mutual-isotopy classification statement for a real curve of degree k together with an M-quartic under the oval-snake hypothesis. Restricted to that configuration. Not a classification of M-curves.
events.remains: All other mutual arrangements, and the M-curve configuration question.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper in vol. 119, issue 2, 2026, per a search summary; the journal page was not opened.

events.direction: Positive isotopy result on a restricted configuration; neighbouring to M-curves but not about M-curve configurations.
events.object: The model curve Q, a small perturbation of a doubled conic, with the theorem that R S4 union R C4 is isotopic to R Q union R C4 under the oval-snake hypothesis. Constructive model; the isotopy is a topological statement from the paper.

events.what_happened: Zoe Geiselmann, Michael Joswig, Lars Kastner, Konrad Mundinger, Sebastian Pokutta, Christoph Spiegel, Marcel Wack and Max Zimmer, '121 Patchworked Curves of Degree Seven' (arXiv 2602.06888 v1, submitted 6 Feb 2026; later retitled 'Limits of combinatorial patchworking'). For each of Viro's 121 real schemes of smooth plane degree-7 curves the paper gives one combinatorial patchwork (a regular unimodular triangulation of 7 times the triangle, with a sign distribution) whose T-curve realises that scheme, and it answers a question of Itenberg and Viro (1996). The v1 abstract is about degree 7 only; the current abstract also treats degree 8 (see the event dated 27 Jul 2026).
events.revisions: v1 6 Feb 2026 (title '121 Patchworked Curves of Degree Seven'); v2 23 Feb 2026; v3 27 Jul 2026; v4 31 Aug 2026 (title 'Limits of combinatorial patchworking'). v2 was not read.
events.delivers: Every real scheme of degree 7 (all smooth curves, including degree-7 M-schemes) is realised by a T-curve. Restriction: T-curves, i.e. combinatorial patchworks, not all algebraic curves. Degree-7 configurations were already known to be realisable by algebraic curves (Brugallé's 2004 arXiv abstract concerns symmetric curves of degree 7; the statement for all 121 schemes was not confirmed in a primary source), so this confirms a construction rather than adding a configuration. No new M-configuration beyond degree 7.
events.remains: Degree 8 and higher. T-curve realisability is a different question from algebraic realisability for the bullet's purposes.
events.directly_checkable: Each T-curve is given by a triangulation of 7 times the triangle plus a sign assignment on its lattice points. Its real scheme is computed combinatorially by the algorithm in arXiv 2604.09221 and by the C++ library libisotopy (polymake). This is software computation, not a formal proof.
events.direction: Positive: every degree-7 scheme is realised as a T-curve. Cuts toward existence for the degree-7 configurations, which were already known to be realised.
events.object: For each of the 121 real schemes of smooth degree-7 plane curves, a patchwork of the dilated triangle 7 times the triangle (a regular unimodular triangulation with signs) whose T-curve has that real scheme. Explicit combinatorial construction, with the scheme identified by computer. Not a non-constructive existence proof.

events.what_happened: Enzo Pasquereau, 'On the Topology of T-manifolds of Higher Codimension' (arXiv 2602.14988, submitted 16 Feb 2026). Gives new bounds on the number of components of T-curves and T-surfaces, and a codimension-2 description of Viro's patchworking that yields a family of maximal real algebraic curves in RP^3.
events.delivers: A family of maximal real algebraic curves in RP^3 (not plane curves), and component bounds for T-curves. Restricted to RP^3 and to T-curves. Not about plane M-curves.
events.remains: Plane M-curves of every degree.
events.direction: Neighbouring: existence of maximal curves in RP^3. No bearing on plane M-configurations.
events.object: A family of maximal real algebraic curves in RP^3 built by codimension-2 patchworking. The construction was described at abstract level only.

events.what_happened: Alois Demory (Universitat Tubingen), talk 'Primitive combinatorial patchworking and real plane curves of degree 8', Seminaire Geometrie enumerative, IMJ-PRG, 3 April 2026. Per the talk abstract: all arrangements up to degree 7 are realisable by primitive combinatorial patchworking; Itenberg's first counterexample for general patchworking is in degree 36; building on B. Haas's results, the speaker shows that already in degree 8 some arrangements of connected components cannot be obtained by primitive combinatorial patchworking. No arXiv or journal write-up was found. The same author's arXiv 2601.07751 (Jan 2026) is a different paper (see dead ends).
events.delivers: Claimed in the talk abstract: some degree-8 arrangements of components are not realisable by primitive combinatorial patchworking; degree 7 and below are fully realisable by that method. Restricted to primitive patchworking, a restricted construction method. Does not address algebraic realisability.
events.remains: Algebraic realisability of degree-8 configurations, and realisability by non-primitive patchworking.
events.doubts: No written argument was found, so the claim rests on the abstract alone. The abstract's phrase 'arrangements of connected components' does not say whether it concerns M-curves only or all degree-8 curves.
events.direction: Obstruction, for a restricted construction method, in degree 8. Does not decide algebraic realisability of M-configurations.

events.what_happened: Geiselmann, Joswig, Kastner, Mundinger, Pokutta, Spiegel, Wack and Zimmer, 'Fast Isotopy Computation for T-Curves' (arXiv 2604.09221, submitted 10 Apr 2026; math.AG, cs.CG, math.CO; one version). Gives a near-quadratic-time algorithm extracting the real scheme of a T-curve from its triangulation and signs, a GPU implementation that computes billions of real schemes per second, and reports that it was used to construct all 121 real schemes of degree 7 by T-curves. The introduction says degree eight remains open, citing Orevkov.
events.delivers: A computational method and an enumeration. For the bullet it reproduces the degree-7 T-curve realisability of the earlier paper and adds no new configuration. Restricted to T-curves.
events.remains: Degree-8 and higher configurations.
events.directly_checkable: The algorithm and its C++ implementation (libisotopy, polymake) can be rerun on given T-curve data.
events.direction: Tool paper; supports the degree-7 positive realisation. No obstruction or realisation claim at degree 8 in what I read.

events.what_happened: Giacomo Maletto, 'Hilbert's 16th problem for arrangements of curves on a surface' (arXiv 2606.21449, submitted 19 Jun 2026; math.AG, math.CO; 38 pages, 21 figures; one version found). It introduces a combinatorial structure (n, W, T) encoding the topological type of a curve crossing a fixed arrangement of curves on a compact real surface, and applies it to a generalisation of Hilbert's 16th problem for arrangements. Results: Theorem B, 119 topological types for three unlabelled lines and a cubic (complete classification); Theorem C, 619 types for three lines and a quartic consisting of a single oval (complete for that case), with bounds of 9426 to 17624 types for three lines and a quartic in general. Methods: Bezout-type obstructions, Viro's patchworking and translations, and the Julia library NWT. A KTH seminar talk on 20 Jan 2026 ('Hilbert's 16th problem for arrangements of a quartic curve and three lines') presented the same material before the write-up, so it is dated here to the write-up. The paper's section 1.2.1 lists the status of single M-curves: d = 4 six types; d = 6 Gudkov 1969; d = 7 Viro; 'd = 8: still open, though much is known'; d >= 9 largely incomplete. The paper's AI disclosure is in section 1.4 (see ai).
events.revisions: v1 only, per the arXiv abstract page read.
events.delivers: A complete classification of arrangements of three lines with a cubic (119 types) and of three lines with a single-oval quartic (619 types), plus bounds for the general three-lines-quartic case. Restricted to arrangements of curves with coordinate lines (or on a surface); does not classify the components of any single M-curve. Establishes realisability through patchworking and necessity through combinatorial Bezout.
events.remains: The configurations of single M-curves of degree 8 and above (listed as open in the paper's own section 1.2.1). The general three-lines-quartic case beyond the single-oval case, and arrangements with other curves.
events.directly_checkable: The 119 and 619 types are produced by the NWT Julia library (archived on Zenodo, cited in the paper); combinatorial curves in the (n, W, T) encoding can be recomputed with it. No proof assistant was reported to be used.
events.doubts: The author states that ChatGPT helped in finding proofs of some topological lemmas (see ai). No external reading has been posted in the roughly four months since v1, and I found no comment or review. This is a fact about the record, not an identified error.
events.direction: Positive: complete classification of two arrangement cases and bounds for a third, with realisability via patchworking. Does not settle the single-M-curve question; the paper itself lists degree 8 as open.
events.object: No single exhibited object. The output is the list of 119 topological types of arrangements of three lines and a cubic and 619 types for a single-oval quartic and three lines, each realised by Viro-type patchworks and checked for necessity by Bezout-type combinatorics.

systems.name: ChatGPT
systems.what_it_did: Per the authors: 'ChatGPT was also helpful for coming up with the proofs of some of the topological lemmas.' Within the sentence on generative AI models, also listed as used to implement some small code functions, research the literature, assist with the writing and proof-reading, and for finding a realization to a particular combinatorial curve (§7.3). The sentence does not say which of the two models found the §7.3 realisation.
systems.basis_quote: The generative AI models ChatGPT and Claude were used to implement some small code functions, research the literature, assist with the writing, proof-reading and for finding a realization to a particular combinatorial curve (§7.3). ChatGPT was also helpful for coming up with the proofs of some of the topological lemmas.

systems.name: Claude
systems.what_it_did: Per the authors, within the sentence on generative AI models: used to implement some small code functions, research the literature, assist with the writing and proof-reading, and for finding a realization to a particular combinatorial curve (§7.3). The sentence does not say whether Claude found that realisation or only helped with other parts.
systems.basis_quote: The generative AI models ChatGPT and Claude were used to implement some small code functions, research the literature, assist with the writing, proof-reading and for finding a realization to a particular combinatorial curve (§7.3). ChatGPT was also helpful for coming up with the proofs of some of the topological lemmas.

events.what_happened: S. Yu. Orevkov, 'On arrangements of plane real quartics with respect to three lines' (arXiv 2607.19457, v1 21 Jul 2026; v2 4 Aug 2026, correcting figures and misprints). Completes the classification of how a smooth real algebraic or pseudoholomorphic quartic sits relative to three lines, assuming each oval meets the lines. It shows one arrangement is realisable pseudoholomorphically but not algebraically, built by patchworking on an irregular triangulation, as the first patchwork example of a PL curve whose arrangement with the coordinate axes is algebraically unrealisable. It continues Maletto's preprint.
events.delivers: Classification of arrangements of a smooth quartic with three lines under the hypothesis that each oval meets the lines, with one arrangement shown pseudoholomorphic but not algebraic. Restricted to arrangements with lines; not M-curves.
events.remains: Arrangements without the oval-meets-lines hypothesis, and single M-curves.
events.direction: Algebraic non-realisability of one arrangement (line-quartic scope). Neighbouring, not an M-curve result.
events.object: One arrangement of a smooth real quartic with three lines, realised as a PL curve by patchworking on an irregular triangulation, realisable pseudoholomorphically but not algebraically. Described at abstract level; details not read.

events.what_happened: Later version of arXiv 2602.06888 (same team as the 6 Feb event). The v3 text states that in degree d = 8 there are M-curves not realisable as T-curves: 'In degree d=8 there are MM-curves not realizable as T-curves.' (as rendered in the HTML; the doubled M is the rendering of the maximal-curve symbol). The current abstract says: 'there are real plane algebraic curves of degree eight that cannot be realized as T-curves'. A summary of the abstract page says this includes several maximal (M-curve) real schemes. The v1 abstract does not contain this claim. v2 (23 Feb 2026) was not read, so the first version carrying the claim is v3 if v2 lacks it, otherwise v2.
events.revisions: Claim absent from v1 abstract. First seen in v3 (27 Jul 2026); v2 (23 Feb 2026) not read. v4 (31 Aug 2026) per the abstract page.
events.delivers: Obstruction: some degree-8 real plane schemes, including several maximal (M) schemes, are not realisable by T-curves (combinatorial patchworks). Restricted to T-curves: it says nothing about realisability by general algebraic M-curves, which is what the bullet asks. The degree-7 result carries over.
events.remains: Whether the non-T-realisable M-schemes are realised by algebraic M-curves, which the paper does not settle. The seven pseudoholomorphic realisations of Orevkov are untouched.
events.doubts: The non-realisability proof was not read: the PDF could not be decoded, and the HTML v3 was read only for its first 100,000 of 162,733 characters. The named schemes are not visible in what was read.
events.direction: Cuts against realisation of some degree-8 M-schemes by T-curves. Does not bear on algebraic realisability; not a counterexample to the bullet's problem.

disputes.summary: Degree 8 is 'open' in Wikipedia (current lead), in Maletto 2026 (section 1.2.1), and in the ZIB NeuCurves project page, but Orevkov's 2002 classification (pseudo-holomorphic) is described as complete for degree 8. The conflict is largely one of setting (algebraic versus pseudo-holomorphic realisability) and is not resolved by the sources read.
The year of Viro's degree-7 classification: 1979 (Maletto 2026, section 1.2.1) versus 1984 (Geiselmann et al. 2026 v1). Original papers not read.
A search summary of Orevkov's 2002 degree-8 table credits Hilbert with 3 of the degree-8 schemes, while the notes it cites say 4 and state uncertainty about attribution. Secondary; not opened.

Second-part claim (Entropy 2024, quadratic bound for H(n)) against the critiques of Buzzi and Novaes (Nov 2024) and the authors' rebuttal (Dec 2024). Disputed in print on arXiv; no journal correction or further response was found. The second part is not the M-curve bullet.

summary: What was found. The bullet asks which configurations of components M-curves can have, for every degree; the sources read (Wikipedia's current lead, Maletto 2026, Geiselmann et al. 2026, Orevkov's degree-8 page, Demory's talk abstract, the ZIB project page) agree that the full list is known through degree 7, is incomplete at degree 8 and open from degree 9 on, with the caveat that Orevkov's 2002 degree-8 classification is pseudo-holomorphic. The in-window movement is almost all on the degree-7 and degree-8 realisability questions, and it is about T-curves, combinatorial patchworks, or arrangements with lines rather than about algebraic M-curves directly. Concretely: (1) Geiselmann, Joswig, Kastner, Mundinger, Pokutta, Spiegel, Wack and Zimmer (arXiv 2602.06888, 6 Feb 2026) realise all 121 degree-7 real schemes by T-curves, with the algorithm and enumeration in arXiv 2604.09221 (10 Apr 2026); (2) in v3 (27 Jul 2026) the same paper asserts that some degree-8 M-curves are not realisable as T-curves, which says nothing about algebraic realisability; (3) Demory's talk of 3 Apr 2026 claims the same kind of obstruction for primitive combinatorial patchworking, with no written argument found; (4) Maletto (arXiv 2606.21449, 19 Jun 2026) classifies arrangements of three lines with a cubic (119 types) and a single-oval quartic (619 types), and Orevkov (arXiv 2607.19457, Jul 2026) completes quartic-with-three-lines arrangements, one of them algebraically unrealisable; neither is about single M-curves, and Maletto's paper still calls degree 8 open. The AI finding: Maletto's section 1.4, 'Acknowledgments and AI usage', states that 'The generative AI models ChatGPT and Claude were used to implement some small code functions, research the literature, assist with the writing, proof-reading and for finding a realization to a particular combinatorial curve (§7.3). ChatGPT was also helpful for coming up with the proofs of some of the topological lemmas.' This is the only system-involvement statement I found for the M-curve problem. Its scope is the arrangement classification, not M-curves, and the source does not say which model found the §7.3 realisation. Its lemma-proof contribution is the one I would expect a later pass to weigh. No other source read names an AI system: the Geiselmann et al. papers, Orevkov's 2026 paper, Orevkov-Puchkova, Pasquereau, Demory's talk, and the Gasull-Santana and Buzzi-Novaes papers were read, and none contains an AI statement in the text read. A ZIB/MATH+ project (NeuCurves, funded Sep 2025 to Aug 2028) plans to apply neural generative models to triangulations and sign distributions to advance the classification of M-curves; it is an announced programme with no result, so it is recorded here, not as an event. Second part (limit cycles, not the bullet): Gasull and Santana (2024 and 2025) prove structural and lower-bound results with no AI statement; the Entropy paper (Aug 2024) claims H(n) <= 2(n-1)(4(n-1)-2), which Buzzi and Novaes (Nov 2024) refute by growth and counterexample, and the authors' rebuttal (Dec 2024) disputes; the Entropy paper itself was not readable (MDPI 403, DOAJ 403, PMC captcha). Pre-window events that bear on the bullet are recorded above: Gudkov's degree-6 classification (1969), Viro's degree-7 classification (1979 or 1984), Orevkov's degree-8 work (2002, algebraic realisation of one scheme and pseudo-holomorphic classification), and Fiedler-Le Touze's degree-9 partial results (2006 and 2008). Close calls: (a) whether Geiselmann et al.'s degree-8 non-T-realisability is a finding about M-curves at all, since it concerns T-curves; I recorded it as a restricted-method obstruction; (b) whether Demory's talk counts, since no written argument exists; I dated it to the talk; (c) whether Maletto's arrangement classification bears on the bullet, since it concerns arrangements of curves and not single M-curves; I recorded it as neighbouring with its own scope; (d) whether the Entropy claim is an event for this bullet at all, since it is about the second part; recorded with a scope note.
competing_reading: Geiselmann et al. v3 (degree-8 M-schemes not T-realisable) and Demory's talk (degree-8 arrangements not reachable by primitive patchworking) can be read as the first real movement on the degree-8 M-curve question since Orevkov: they are obstructions in 2026 that were not in the sources before 2024. The opposing reading: both are obstructions for restricted constructions (T-curves, primitive patchworks), so they cannot change the status of algebraic M-curves of degree 8, which the sources still list as open; Orevkov's 2002 pseudo-holomorphic classification and Brugallé's six unknown schemes remain the algebraic state of the art. A second contrast: Maletto's paper classifies arrangements that include a cubic or quartic and could be read as a generalisation of the bullet's question, in which case the AI-involved preprint is directly on Hilbert's 16th problem; the opposing reading is that it classifies arrangements with lines, and single M-curves are untouched.
what_would_settle_it: (1) The full text of arXiv 2602.06888 v3 and v4 (degree-8 theorem and its statement about algebraic versus T-realisability), and whether the non-T-realisable schemes are among the six Brugallé/Orevkov schemes whose algebraic status is open. (2) Demory's written paper, if any, stating the degree-8 non-realisability theorem and its class (M-curves or all curves). (3) Orevkov's GAFA paper (year and content), and any later source that resolves the six degree-8 schemes. (4) The Entropy paper's primary text and any journal correction, which would settle the second-part dispute (not the M-curve bullet). (5) Maletto's section 7.3 and the authorship of the §7.3 realisation, to decide which model (if either) produced a load-bearing mathematical object. (6) The full text of Maletto's proofs of topological lemmas, to see what the AI-assisted lemmas establish and whether they are used in the classification.

arXiv 2601.07751 (Demory, Jan 2026): real critical points of T-polynomials and topology of T-hypersurfaces in P^n; not plane curves, no degree-8 claim in the abstract read.

arXiv 2603.16283 (Rocchi, Safey El Din, Mar 2026): computing connected components of real algebraic curves; a computational method, not a configuration result for M-curves; not opened.
Ragsdale's conjecture on even ovals (counterexamples by Itenberg; dates given as 1979 by Wikipedia and 1993 by Itenberg sources): concerns non-maximal curves, outside the bullet.
Harnack curves (Mikhalkin, Annals 2000, arXiv math/0010018): a special class of M-curves in toric surfaces; pre-window and a different class.
Pedregal 2021 arXiv 2103.07193 (second part): an earlier claimed degree-4 polynomial bound on H(n), pre-window, not opened.
Itenberg CIRM 2025 talk on real plane sextics without real singular points (arithmetic-congruence extension): a talk, no paper found, singular curves outside the bullet.
Gudkov-Rokhlin congruence: no 2025 or 2026 arXiv proof found in searches; the classical sources are pre-window.
Lean or Coq formalisation of Hilbert's sixteenth problem or of Harnack's theorem: none found.

incomplete: (1) The Entropy paper (da Silva, Vieira, Leonel, Entropy 2024) was not read: MDPI and DOAJ returned HTTP 403, PMC a reCAPTCHA page; its date and content come from search snippets and the two critiques. Its AI status is therefore unverified (none_found is recorded as true only on the basis of the critiques and snippets). (2) Geiselmann et al. (arXiv 2602.06888): the PDF was not decodable; the HTML v1 was read with truncation; the v3 HTML was read only for its first 100,000 of 162,733 characters, so its acknowledgements may lie in the unread tail; v2 was not read; the non-realisability theorem for degree 8 was not read, so I did not identify the schemes it covers. (3) Maletto (arXiv 2606.21449): the HTML v1 was read in parts (about 100,000 of 154,854 characters); the theorem statements come from the abstract summary and the intro; the PDF was not decodable. (5) Orevkov's 2002 'New M-curve of degree 8' note was not opened; its content comes from search summaries. (6) Viro's and Gudkov's original papers were not opened; their dates and results come from Maletto's and Geiselmann et al.'s introductions and from search summaries. Viro's year is disputed (1979 versus 1984).
